title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Site Ops, Top Issues & Canonical Fixes
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Playbook for Developer Experience documentation: ownership, templates, SDK guides, quickstarts, canonical API examples, docs site operating procedures, and a curated list of top support issues with canonical fixes and rollouts.
body:
Overview

This document codifies the Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation standards and operational playbook for SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and our canonical fixes for top support issues. The intended audience is SDK authors, technical writers, support engineers, and DevEx maintainers.

Goals
- Provide consistent, high-quality SDK guides and API examples that get engineers to a working prototype in under 15 minutes.
- Maintain a small set of canonical quickstarts and templates that are easy to fork and lintable.
- Reduce support volume by documenting top incidents and providing reproducible, tested fixes.
- Ensure docs-site reliability and a clear ops runbook for releases, rollbacks, and content migrations.

Scope
Includes: JavaScript/TypeScript SDK, Python SDK, REST API examples, canonical prompt+eval snippets, quickstarts (chat, embeddings, reranking), docs-site CI/CD procedures, and top support issues related to SDK usage and API errors. Excludes: model research notebooks and team meeting notes (stored in Google Drive).

Contents and Ownership
- Doc owner: DevEx Docs (eng-developer-experience)
- Primary author: Aisha Patel (DevEx Writer)
- Reviewers: Marco Li (SDK), Sofia Nguyen (Support), Priya Kapoor (Platform)
- Publishing cadence: major refresh every quarter; critical fixes within 48 hours.

Standards (applies to all DevEx docs)
1) Style and structure
   - Use short title with kebab-case file name in repo (e.g., developer-experience-sdk-quickstart-chat-2026.md).
   - Start with a 2-3 sentence summary, prerequisites, and a one-command quickstart.
   - Provide a minimal reproducible example first, then expanded examples and troubleshooting.
   - Mark breaking changes with a clear banner and migration steps.

2) Content requirements
   - Example code: Must be copy-paste runnable; include dependency install commands and expected outputs.
   - API endpoints: use canonical base URL https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1 for internal examples, and https://api.redwood.ai/v1 for public examples.
   - Security note: never include live API keys. Use placeholders (REDWOOD_API_KEY).

3) Testing and validation
   - All quickstarts must pass an automated smoke test in docs-site CI (see Docs site operating procedures).
   - SDK examples must include a unit-level snippet checked by SDK maintainers during PR review.

Canonical File Templates (examples)
- Quickstart README template:
  1) Title & TL;DR
  2) Prereqs (SDK version, OS, API key)
  3) One-liner install + one-command run
  4) Minimal example (Python + Node)
  5) Next steps + links

- SDK Guide template:
  - Overview, Installation, Authentication, Basic usage, Advanced usage (streaming, function-calling), Tests & examples, Migration notes, Changelog link.

SDK Guides: concrete guidance
- Python SDK (owner: SDK-python team)
  - Minimum required: examples for text generation, chat completion, embeddings, streaming responses, and error handling (429/backoff).
  - Example snippet (Python):

    ```python
    from redwood import RedwoodClient

    client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDWOOD_API_KEY")
    resp = client.generate(model="redwood-base-13b", prompt="Summarize the following:\n\n- Redwood is a developer-first inference platform.")
    print(resp.text)
    ```

  - Recommended SLO for docs examples: end-to-end example should run in < 5s on CI runner or be mocked.

- JavaScript/TypeScript SDK (owner: SDK-js team)
  - Provide both callback and async/await examples, and one example using streaming responses via EventSource/Fetch streaming.

API Examples (canonical)
- Public REST minimal (curl):

  ```bash
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-base-13b","input":"Write a one paragraph summary of Redwood Inference."}'
  ```

- Response handling guidance: check status codes 200, 400, 401, 429, 5xx. Provide retry/backoff policy (see Top Issues).

Quickstarts and Templates
- Official quickstarts (canonical):
  1) Chat quickstart (Node + Python) — interactive chat UI + streaming example.
  2) Embeddings quickstart — vectorize text, store in Faiss example.
  3) Reranking quickstart — use embeddings + rerank API.
  4) Function-calling quickstart — show structured outputs and type hints.

- Each quickstart must include:
  - CI smoke test steps (./ci/run_quickstart_smoke.sh)
  - Test data under /tests/fixtures and a local development flag (REDWOOD_LOCAL_DEV=1)

Docs site operating procedures (CI/CD & content ops)
- Build pipeline (owner: DevEx infra):
  - Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/devex-docs
  - CI: GitHub Actions job `docs:build` runs on PR, includes link-check, lint, smoke tests.
  - Publishing: Merge to main triggers `docs:deploy` to staging; QA team must sign off before promoting to production.

- Release checklist for content changes:
  1) Add changelog entry in docs-changelog.yml
  2) Run `make docs-smoke` locally or in CI — all quickstarts must pass.
  3) Assign reviewer (SDK owner + Support lead).
  4) After merge, monitor docs-site health dashboard (Grafana board `devex.docs.health`) for 24 hours.

- Rollback procedure:
  - If staging or prod build fails, revert the merge commit and re-run `docs:deploy` for the last green tag. Notify #devex-docs on Slack and create a P0 ticket in Jira.

Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes (curated list)
- ISSUE-101: "401 Unauthorized" in SDK examples
  - Symptom: Copy-paste example returns 401.
  - Root cause: User used live key or omitted Bearer prefix; or organization key lacks role.
  - Canonical fix: Update quickstart to show `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...` and code to validate header: `Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY`.
  - Owner: Support + SDK teams.

- ISSUE-112: "429 Too Many Requests" during CI smoke tests
  - Symptom: Intermittent 429s causing flaky docs CI runs.
  - Root cause: Tests hit hosted API rate limits or tests run in parallel without mock.
  - Canonical fix: Use recorded fixtures for CI; if live test required, add client-side exponential backoff with jitter and rate-limit headers check. Update CI to run live tests in a serialized `docs:live-tests` job with quota tag.
  - Owner: DevEx infra + Support.

- ISSUE-127: "Streaming socket disconnect" in JS streaming example
  - Symptom: Streaming response aborted on some browsers/CI runners.
  - Root cause: Improper use of Fetch streaming; examples used `response.body.getReader()` without backpressure logic.
  - Canonical fix: Provide an EventSource-based fallback and a robust reader example with backpressure handling; include a note about proxies/load-balancers terminating idle connections.
  - Owner: SDK-js team.

- ISSUE-138: "Embeddings mismatch / dimension error"
  - Symptom: Downstream FAISS indexing fails with dimension mismatch.
  - Root cause: Mismatch between the embeddings model used in quickstart and the vector store config.
  - Canonical fix: Add explicit model pin in quickstart (e.g., `model: redwood-embed-2k`) and include a small validation snippet: `assert len(vector) == 1536` (or the expected dimension).
  - Owner: Applied ML & DevEx.

Process for triage and canonicalization
1) Support engineer files a PR with a failing test and a proposed doc change.
2) Tag SDK owner and Support lead; include a short repro (curl + expected output).
3) If change is low-risk (typo, missing header), merge after one reviewer. If it changes behavior or examples, run smoke tests and get two reviewers.
4) After merge, close related support ticket and add entry to the public troubleshooting page.

Metrics and KPIs
- Time-to-first-success: median time for a new user to run a quickstart to completion; target < 15 minutes.
- Docs CI green rate: > 98% (weekly).
- Reduction in support tickets mapped to top issues: aim for 50% reduction YOY after canonicalization.

Appendix: Example smoke test (bash)

  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -euo pipefail
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY="${REDWOOD_API_KEY:-testkey}"
  echo "Running chat quickstart smoke..."
  python quickstarts/chat/smoke_test.py --api-url=https://staging-api.redwood.ai \
     || { echo 'Smoke failed' ; exit 1; }
  echo "Smoke passed"
